tools.name: list_tunnels
tools.description: List the user's Pipehero tunnels and whether each is currently online.

tools.name: list_requests
tools.description: List recent webhooks/requests captured for a tunnel. Returns id, method, path, status and bodies.

tools.name: get_request
tools.description: Get the full request and response (headers + body) of one captured webhook by id.

tools.name: replay_request
tools.description: Replay a captured webhook to the user's localhost (the tunnel CLI must be running).

tools.name: send_test_webhook
tools.description: Send a generated test webhook to the user's localhost (the tunnel CLI must be running). Provide a `provider` (stripe, github, shopify, clerk, slack, resend, paddle, polar, lemonsqueezy) and optional `event` for a realistic sample payload, or pass a custom JSON `body`. Pro plan required.

tools.name: set_long_requests
tools.description: Opt a tunnel into a 120-second ingress timeout instead of the 30-second default — for tool calls that legitimately run long, e.g. an MCP server exposed through the tunnel. Persists on the tunnel; pass enabled: false to revert to the 30-second default.

tools.name: set_ws_passthrough
tools.description: Opt a tunnel into WebSocket passthrough, so an application-level WebSocket connection (e.g. a mobile/web app's own realtime feature) can be relayed to your localhost. Pro/Team plan required to enable; pass enabled: false to disable on any plan.

tools.name: list_api_collections
tools.description: List the workspace's API collections (saved endpoints with examples and environments). Start here to find a collection_id.

tools.name: get_api_collection
tools.description: Get one collection's folders, endpoints (id, method, path, name, version, example count) and environments (with their variables).

tools.name: get_api_endpoint
tools.description: Get one endpoint in full: description, parameters, headers, request body, saved response examples and its current `version`. Identify it by endpoint_id or by method + path.

tools.name: create_api_collection
tools.description: Create an empty API collection. Prefer import_api_spec when there is an OpenAPI file, and upsert_api_endpoint to fill it from the code.

tools.name: upsert_api_endpoint
tools.description: Document an endpoint: creates it, or updates the existing one for the same method + path. Use it whenever you add or change a route in the code, so the docs stay true. tools.name: add_api_example
tools.description: Save a response example on an endpoint (for instance the 402 your handler returns for a declined card). Replaces the example with the same name, so it is safe to repeat.

tools.name: delete_api_endpoint
tools.description: Delete an endpoint and its examples. Use when the route no longer exists in the code. Cannot be undone.

tools.name: import_api_spec
tools.description: Import an OpenAPI 3.x document (as JSON), a Postman v2.x collection (JSON) or a curl command into a new collection, or into `collection_id`. All or nothing, and plan limits are checked first. Credentials are never imported (they become variables). Convert YAML to JSON before sending.

tools.name: export_api_collection
tools.description: Export a collection as an OpenAPI 3.1 or Postman 2.1 document. Handy to read the whole API at once.

tools.name: run_api_endpoint
tools.description: Send an endpoint against an environment and return the real response (status, headers, body up to 20 KB). tools.description: Document a real request captured by a tunnel (get its id from list_requests). If an endpoint already covers the route, the response is added to it as an example; otherwise an endpoint is created from the request. Credentials, cookies and signatures are replaced by {{variables}} and only JSON bodies

tools.name: list_api_monitors
tools.description: See which endpoints of a collection are checked on a schedule (Pro/Team monitors) and how they are doing: state (healthy, failing, blip, paused, waiting), the last check with its status, latency and error, and since when it has been failing. Use it to find out what is broken in staging or production

tools.name: list_api_proposals
tools.description: See what happened to the changes you proposed. Some workspaces review AI changes: your write tools then answer `pending_review` and change nothing until a teammate approves. This lists the latest proposals with their status (pending, approved, rejected with the reviewer's reason, or failed with why)

tools.description: Compare a collection's docs with the real traffic a tunnel captured (Pro/Team). tools.description: Recent runs of an endpoint (newest first, default 5): who/what was sent and what came back. Use to see what happened the last time it was run.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_api_proposals · Private data: create_api_collection, upsert_api_endpoint, import_api_spec, export_api_collection, save_captured_request · Public sink: get_request, replay_request, send_test_webhook, upsert_api_endpoint, run_api_endpoint · Destructive: set_long_requests, delete_api_endpoint, run_api_endpoint, list_api_runs.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_api_proposals · Private data: create_api_collection, upsert_api_endpoint, import_api_spec, export_api_collection, save_captured_request · Public sink: get_request, replay_request, send_test_webhook, upsert_api_endpoint, run_api_endpoint · Destructive: set_long_requests, delete_api_endpoint, run_api_endpoint, list_api_runs

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
